newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rebel Kurds clash with troops in eastern Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Kurds clash with troops in eastern Turkey.

text.p: Rebel Kurds clashed with Turkish troops in the eastern town of Tunceli on Tuesday after the rebels attacked a police post, military officials said.

"They attacked around 1 a.m. (2200 GMT) and the clashes lasted three hours," an army official told Reuters. "The bodies of two PKK (Kurdistan Workers Party guerrillas) were found in a search of the area after the clashes."
Security forces with mortar bombs and armoured vehicles countered the PKK attack and the rebels fled into the countryside after the fighting.
Up to 20,000 troops backed by air power on Monday launched a drive against Kurdish rebels in the remote mountains of Tunceli province.
Military officials said about 250 PKK rebels were cornered in a forest near the Ahvanos valley in Tunceli, and government troops killed six Kurdish fighters in the clashes.
There was no word on casualties among security forces.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the 12-year fight between Turkish troops and the PKK, which is fighting for independence or autonomy in southeast Turkey.
